notes: A decimal real literal keeps its apparent scale 'unless the value is rounded or the value is zero (in which latter case the sign and scale will be 0)' (PDF p. 73 lines 9-14), so 0.000000m is the decimal with sign 0, coefficient 0 and scale 0. The zero exception is explicit 1st-edition text and the 7th edition's 6.4.5.4 drops it ('preserved unless the value is rounded', PDF p. 54); the observer Decimal.GetBits belongs to the library the 1st edition incorporates by reference (PDF p. 389 lines 2-6; listed at PDF p. 407 line 15), with its bit representation checked by the nonzero decimal control. The 0.731000m mutant keeps scale 6 under the 1st edition and fails, isolating the zero value. Positive witnesses establish prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity.

notes: line-indicator is 'decimal-digits whitespace file-name' with no stated maximum (PDF p. 82 lines 24-27), and for a non-default indicator 'the compiler treats the line after the directive as having the given line number (and file name, if specified)' (PDF p. 82 lines 35-37). The decimal-digits line indicator has no numeric cap in this edition. The required warning coordinate is the supplied line number; the pinned diagnostic uses a different coordinate.

quote_json: "If the operand of the negation operator is of type uint, it is converted to type long, and the type of the result is long."
notes: An unsuffixed literal takes the first of int, uint, long, ulong that holds its value (PDF p. 72 lines 13-15), the int -2147483648 exception covers only a decimal-integer-literal (PDF p. 72 lines 25-29), and negating a uint operand converts it to long with a long result, the exception again being only the decimal literal (PDF p. 169 lines 3-5). 0x80000000 is uint, so -0x80000000 is a long constant; no implicit constant conversion takes long to int (PDF p. 129 lines 6-11), so only Pick(long) applies and returns 2. The 7th edition's 6.4.5.3 widens the exception to any Integer_Literal (PDF p. 53) while its 12.9.3 still says decimal (PDF p. 257); that later change does not reach ISO-1, and the decimal mutant must select Pick(int) and fail. Positive witnesses establish prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity. At ISO-2, ECMA-334 4th ed 14.6.2, p. 194 (PDF p. 216) requires this result. The unsuffixed hexadecimal operand is uint and its negation is long. The lexical minimum exception is expressly decimal. Selecting the int overload contradicts the fourth requirement.

At ISO-1, int \u005fslot = 8; is a compile-time error, because no identifier-start-character matches an escape for U+005F; the literal repair _slot compiles and prints 8. Use the short \u005f spelling as the witness: the 7th-edition grammar also omits \U0000005F, so the long spelling (also an error at ISO-1) does not isolate the 1st/7th difference. At ISO-2, ECMA-334 4th ed 9.4.2, p. 70 (PDF p. 92) requires this result. The initial escape represents Pc underscore, not a permitted letter escape. The separate underscore production contains the literal character. The fourth grammar requires rejection; the literal-underscore witness removes this fault.

The pinned compiler treats the potential angle span before ampersand as a generic name and rejects the local identifiers as generic/type arguments. The third-edition closed follower list excludes ampersand and instead permits the two relational arguments, including the pointer/address-of comparison. Parenthesizing the two arguments preserves their operands, pointer operations and call while avoiding the disputed parse. Positive construct witnesses establish prerequisites; these failures do not establish mutation sensitivity. At ISO-1 the same ordinary relational argument pair is rejected with CS8022 as though generic syntax were required; it declares no generic type or method. The pointer/address witness executes successfully.

quote_json: "White space is defined as any character with Unicode class Zs (which includes the space character)"
notes: The fourth edition's dated reference in clause 3, p. 5 (PDF p. 27), binds Unicode 4.0. Its 4.0.0 category data classifies both U+200B and U+205F as Zs. Therefore 9.3.3 requires U+200B as white space at ISO-2. The compiler rejects it with CS1056 and CS1003. The third-edition U+205F rejection claim is superseded at ISO-2, where the fourth-edition replacement requires acceptance. The ASCII-space construct witness compiles. Replacing U+200B with U+205F does not establish ISO-2 mutation sensitivity.
